title: M0: Land the architecture skeleton with build checks and CI
body:
## Parent

#36 (Spec: Lexicon v0)

**Milestone:** M0  
**User stories:** 109, 110  
**Test seam:** pure seam (build and import checks)  
**Modules:** all module targets (skeleton), Package.swift, build scripts, CI

## What to build

Bring the compiling type sketch from branch `architecture/app-stack` onto main as the M0 starting skeleton: the 15 module targets, the app shell and `lexicon-eval`. The `lexicon` hook CLI is not built (no hooks before the after-M1 grill). Build rules that keep parallel builders from colliding:

- Every build runs `swift build` with the explicit target dependency import check set to error, plus the import-check script that catches transitive imports and bans SwiftUI and Combine everywhere.
- A check script runs build, import check and `swift test` with the extra framework and rpath flags Command Line Tools need.
- One macOS CI job per push and PR running the check script, unsigned or ad-hoc. One check name, which the Reviewer waits on.
- Swift 6 language mode, strict concurrency, internal imports by default, macOS 26 minimum. FluidAudio declared only for the local model target.

Change the sketch's defaults to the spec: race cutoff 300 ms after recording stops, Cleanup deadline about 450 ms, local Parakeet as the M0 engine, up to 50 Terms to speech and 200 to Cleanup, 10-minute model linger, AI cleanup on (inert until M3), start at login on.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `swift build` with the import check passes on main under Command Line Tools 26.6.
- [ ] Adding `import SwiftUI` to any target fails the check script.
- [ ] `swift test` runs through the check script.
- [ ] CI runs the check script on every push and PR and reports one check.
- [ ] The shared preference defaults match the values above.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately)

title: M0: Bootstrap the Glox workflow into Lexicon
body:
## Parent

#36 (Spec: Lexicon v0)

**Milestone:** M0  
**User stories:** 108, 109  
**Test seam:** none (workflow files; verified by a dry run)  
**Modules:** repo workflow only

## What to build

Bring Jake's orchestrator / builders / reviewer workflow from the Glox repo (`~/code/glox-brain-lab`, read-only reference) into Lexicon, adapted for a Swift app and **local Claude Code only**: no cloud builders, and **only the Reviewer merges**.

- **Roles:** Jake decides (grills, approvals, "install"). One long-running orchestrator (keeps the map, writes specs, tickets and builder prompts, starts builders, never merges). Builders, one ticket (or an approved sequence) each, in their own worktree. A Reviewer session that Jake and the orchestrator spin off when PRs need review (Opus high); it reviews green PRs against a review checklist, gives one verdict, and merges its own merge verdicts one at a time with a head-sha-pinned squash merge, only on green CI and only when the branch isn't behind main. No Deployer: the Reviewer takes that job. On Jake's "install", it runs the daily install command (which waits if a Dictation is in progress); nobody installs without his word.
- **Models:** orchestrator, builders and Reviewer on Opus high. Builders fan out to Haiku 5.5 xhigh helpers (scouts, editors on disjoint files, critics per review section, verifiers per finding), sized up to about 15 on a hard ticket; helpers may start their own helpers; Sonnet or Opus subagents where judgment matters. Builders run every commit, push, GitHub write and heavy build themselves, once.
- **Concurrency:** up to 8 builders at once to start (Jake, 2026-10-11), raised only if disk, memory and the CI queue hold up. Builders that edit the same files don't run side by side. Only one builder at a time drives the live app (fn, mic, paste, Accessibility): a single live-app lane. Worktrees share one SwiftPM cache, and a merged ticket's worktree and build folder are deleted. GitHub allows 5 concurrent macOS CI jobs on this repo.
- **Carry over and adapt:** the generic parts of AGENTS.md; docs/agents workflow and review checklist (rewritten for Swift and Lexicon's risks: audio capture, History, insertion, network access, private data); the implement-ticket skill (minus cloud parts) and PR skill (`Refs #N` alone on the first line, never a closing keyword, Merge Danger, `Check:` line; "Deploy" becomes "Install"); the orchestrator-handoff skill; the four helper agents; the guard hook; labels with the status as each comment's first line; merge main into branches, never rebase. Rewrite anything that imported Glox's code on plain `gh` (`gh pr checks --watch`, `gh pr merge --squash --match-head-commit`). The Reviewer waits on the single CI check that "Land the architecture skeleton" creates.
- **Already decided, fold in:** builders launch the app with `open`; dev builds use the Lexicon Dev bundle ID and data folder and never touch the daily copy's permissions; private data (Wispr export, Test set, starter Lexicon, keys) is never committed or sent anywhere the spec doesn't allow; copy only MIT/Apache/BSD code with copyright lines, GPL ideas only. Update CLAUDE.md's subagent model section to the rules above.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and docs/agents describe the local-only roles, the model rules, the live-app lane and that only the Reviewer merges.
- [ ] The skills, helper agents and guard hook exist; the guard refuses a builder's push or merge to main (shown by a dry run).
- [ ] A dry run on a throwaway ticket goes ticket → worktree → PR → Reviewer verdict, without merging (the CI wait is wired to the check name from the skeleton ticket).
- [ ] Nothing private is referenced except by its path under `~/Library/Application Support/Lexicon/`.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately)
